title: High-Volume Batch Inference Pipeline
subtitle: Classify 100 million records before 6 a.m., make every retry harmless, and agree in advance what ships when the run falls behind.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Contract and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Restate the target, ask the partial-result question and name who owns each decision.

practice_prompts.label: Sizing from the deadline
practice_prompts.hint: Derive records/s with headroom, tokens per run and the quota that really limits you.

practice_prompts.label: Architecture and replay
practice_prompts.hint: Draw both planes, then explain why a crash after the sink write cannot create a duplicate.

practice_prompts.label: Failure policy and 4 a.m.
practice_prompts.hint: Classify failures, find the bottleneck and name the pre-agreed contingency and its owner.

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: Pick the scorecard metrics and the gates from benchmark to 10% load.

rubric: Restates the prompt as a replayable, cost-controlled batch by deadline and asks the partial-result question before drawing.
Derives about 4,630 records/s, 5,320 with 15% headroom, and 27B tokens per run, and sizes from the tail rather than the mean.
Keys results on job_id, record_id and model_version and explains why model_version is in the key.
Orders the worker as sink write, then checkpoint, then lease acknowledgement, and traces a crash between write and checkpoint.
Places backpressure and the cost ceiling in the rate-limit coordinator so a quota cut slows leases instead of causing a retry storm.
Classifies failures as fail closed, degrade, queue or human intervention, and separates transient retries from quarantine.
Answers the 45%-at-4-a.m. case by finding the bottleneck first and using only a contingency mode agreed with a named owner.
Gates rollout on a representative token benchmark, 1% and 10% load tests and a rehearsed crash after the sink write.

editorial_review.evidence: Read all 49 captured sections of the batch pipeline source (intro, interview guide, six deep-dive topics, cheat sheet and the five-part full design) and mapped each to the new structure in 90 item-level rows. The guide and full design repeated the sizing, architecture and 4 a.m. material; these were consolidated into eleven walkthrough steps that keep both versions' distinct details (the guide's 2k RPM, EU residency and 8k-token examples alongside the full design's eleven-axis table; the guide's Reliability and Operability targets merged into the full design's testable NFR table). Added teaching: a term list in the brief, an illustrative r-1042 record trace, a crash-point table for the write-checkpoint-ack order, an illustrative 4 a.m. rate calculation (7,640 rec/s needed vs 3,125 observed, assuming a midnight start) and a labelled illustrative cost price. Kept the source's attribution of the cost formula and compliance frameworks to a supplementary V2 author. The original worksheet was not part of the capture and is not imported; the local worksheet is labelled as an addition.
